rules_bindings.description: Axiom rules bindings for the New Zealand v0 graph build. Each binding names one rulespec-nz module by repository-relative rulespec_path and SHA-256 at the pinned commit, the Frame entity it runs on, the period label it runs for, and the variables the graph requests. build_transport_registry (transport/registry.py) builds one AxiomEngine per binding, and one simulate.rules_by_ref@1 router serves them all, because a run's kernel registry holds one kernel per ref. A binding that declares no relations goes through assert_no_relations, which refuses a module whose dense program on the binding's entity declares relations; every bound module declares none at the pin. No kernel implementation hash is to bind the whole NZ spec.

rulespec.verification: The commit is the merge of rulespec-nz PR #122 and is contained in origin/main (git branch -r --contains). The tree is exported with git archive, so the graph source carries no .git directory.

engine.status: Pinned for G8-x (D1 method card MC1). commit is the axiom-rules-engine commit that NZ's input surface and input closure record. wheel_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the dense-extension wheel the NZ hub built at that commit (maturin build --release --locked; CPython 3.14, macOS arm64). axiom_engine_ref records both as declared and hashes no installed wheel.

input_surface.notes: The committed input surface was generated at rulespec-nz 6fe181fc (the fixture records the full commit), an ancestor of the pinned commit on main; git diff 6fe181fc 8dc2507 is empty for every bound module, so the SHA-256 values agree. root_input_count is the size of each module's canonical input surface.

bindings.notes: Entitlement predicates only; the weekly rates and income-test reductions live in the rates module. Undetermined judgments feed take-up through the G4 input-closure table.
Also evaluated by the reg 17/18 bridge (as_rate_bridge.json) under declared input overrides.
NZ Superannuation eligibility for the O4-calibrated receipt layer (MC6).

The module takes the reg 17 base rate and reg 18 non-beneficiary cutout as inputs (its summary: "for later cross-module wiring"); as_rate_bridge.json supplies them until rulespec-nz encodes regs 17 and 18. Calibration-tier variants add their own AS nodes.

Used only for the eldest-child family tax credit amount in the reg 17 base rate. The module also declares 4 rules on an engine Child entity that the NZ schema does not map; the bridge requests none of them, and G1/G7 must show the adapter compiles the module under that condition or stop. The G8-w4 review ran the real engine, at the commit the input closure's input_surface.engine names, against the pinned rulespec commit above and the input-surface commit: the output returned 7921 with only the two care-unit inputs at 1 and 0 and the other 15 Family roots at arbitrary values, dropping either input raised missing input, AxiomEngine.variables() listed the 17 Family roots and no Child name, and simulate.counterfactual@1 delivered both inputs as overrides with neither column on the frame. A second walk over the engine's parsed model reached exactly the two inputs.

unreached_roots.reason: family_tax_credit_prescribed_amount reads only the eldest and subsequent dependent child care units, so no request this binding makes reaches these 15 Family roots. The axiom:nz concept mapping binds in_work_tax_credit_allowed_children_count, but no requested rule reads it, so the input-closure producer drops that binding from the mapping it checks. A binding that requests another output, or a module edit that moves the SHA-256 above, makes the producer refuse until a reviewer re-verifies this list.

bindings.notes: https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-nz/blob/8dc2507d5f10a0467c285fed54d018ee37246798/nz/statutes/income_tax/schedule_1/individual_income_tax.yaml (SHA-256 5ff8e7bf645b85e3d59d612e3c6eb70e09090fb13b40d49c3c5f8a4202e0b82a); https://www.workandincome.govt.nz/products/benefit-rates/benefit-rates-april-2026.html. Each gross-up inverts annualised Schedule 1 before credits over 52 weeks independently of other income, with solver-owned taxable_income and no ACC earners levy. NZ Super supplies before-tax amounts directly; the gross-up never inverts it.

rules_bindings.keying_note: Each Axiom-bound node is to carry its own binding entry, the rulespec and engine pin blocks, the entity names and its period, plus a digest of exactly those values, never this file's SHA-256. Otherwise an Accommodation Supplement edit would re-key the main-benefit and NZ Super nodes, which sit upstream of calibration. Which graph nodes consume which binding is the composer's business, not this resource's.

graph_start.note: The case starts after the packaged transport_graph nodes that write its concept frame: the frame stands in for their outputs. Of those nodes the generator runs only nz.create's unit construction (pipeline.units). writers names the node that writes each column (nz.create where no other node declares it as an output). The four receives_* flags are nz.takeup.assign's output in the graph, not CREATE's; the case states them as placeholders.
